title: Run any command from the Command Palette
summary: Open the Command Palette, find a command by name, and use Quick Open.

steps.say: Click inside the VS Code window so it is in front.
hints: The title bar should say Visual Studio Code.
Press Alt Tab to switch to it.
steps.why: Keyboard shortcuts go to the window that is in front.

steps.say: Press Control Shift P to open the Command Palette.

checks.prompt: Is a search box open at the top center of VS Code, starting with a greater-than sign?

hints: Or open the View menu and choose Command Palette.
steps.why: The Command Palette lists every command, so you never need to hunt through menus.

steps.say: Type color theme, then press Enter on Preferences: Color Theme.

checks.prompt: Is a list of color themes such as Dark Modern and Light Modern showing at the top of VS Code?

hints: You only need part of the name; the list filters as you type.
Use the arrow keys to move through matches before pressing Enter.
steps.why: Searching by name is faster than remembering where a command lives.

steps.say: Move up and down the list to preview themes. Press Enter to keep one, or Escape to cancel.
hints: The window changes color as you move through the list.
Escape puts the old theme back.
steps.why: Previews let you try a setting before committing to it.

steps.say: Now press Control P. This box finds files by name instead of commands.

checks.prompt: Is a search box open at the top center listing recently opened files?

hints: Type a greater-than sign in this box to switch it back to commands.
Press Escape to close the box when you are done.
steps.why: Quick Open is the fastest way to jump between files in a big project.
